# Temple Scroll Column 64 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 64 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**64:1** And the Levite who is within your gates — you shall not forsake him, for he has no portion or inheritance with you.

**64:2** At the end of three years you shall bring out all the tithe of your produce in that year and lay it up within your gates.

**64:3** And the Levite, because he has no portion or inheritance with you, and the sojourner and the orphan and the widow who are within your gates, shall come and eat and be satisfied,

**64:4** so that I may bless you in all the work of your hand that you do.

**64:5** At the end of seven years you shall make a release. And this is the manner of the release: every creditor shall release what he has lent to his neighbor; he shall not exact it of his neighbor or his brother,

**64:6** because the release of the LORD has been proclaimed. Of a foreigner you may exact it, but whatever of yours is with your brother your hand shall release.

**64:7** If a man is found stealing a soul from among his brothers, from among the children of Israel, and he deals tyrannically with him and sells him, then that thief shall die. And you shall purge the evil from your midst.

**64:8** If there is in a man a sin worthy of the judgment of death, and he is put to death, and you hang him upon a tree,

**64:9** his corpse shall not remain overnight upon the tree, but you shall surely bury him on that day, for a hanged one is cursed by God.

**64:10** And you shall not defile your land that I am giving to you as an inheritance.

**64:11** If a man informs against his people and delivers his people to a foreign nation and does evil against his people,

**64:12** you shall hang him on a tree and he shall die. On the testimony of two witnesses and on the testimony of three witnesses

**64:13** he shall be put to death, and they shall hang him on the tree.

---

*EMET notes: Column 64 is the most theologically significant column in 11QT. Lines 64:6–13 rework Deut 21:22–23 but with a revolutionary addition: lines 64:11–13 describe hanging ALIVE as a form of execution for treason — betraying one's people to a foreign nation. In Deuteronomy, hanging is post-mortem display; in the Temple Scroll, it is execution itself. This passage was central to debates about crucifixion in Second Temple Judaism and is referenced in 4QpNahum's commentary on Alexander Jannaeus's crucifixion of 800 Pharisees. "A sin worthy of the judgment of death" (משפט מות) preserved literally. "Informs against" for רכל preserves the espionage/betrayal connotation.*
